title: Artificial Intelligence: Council and Parliament agree to simplify and streamline rules
key_claim: Council and European Parliament reach provisional agreement on Digital Omnibus on AI, postponing high-risk AI obligations to 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (embedded products); adds new prohibitions on AI-generated CSAM and non-consensual intimate imagery.
signals_supported: EU AI Act high-risk regime postponement

title: Electricity 2026
key_claim: Global data centre electricity demand grew 17% in 2025; AI-focused data centre consumption surged 50% in 2025; projection that data centre electricity consumption roughly doubles from 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh by 2030, with AI-focused capacity tripling.

title: Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models
key_claim: GPAI obligations entered into application 2 August 2025; Commission enforcement powers and fines for GPAI providers begin 2 August 2026; providers of models on market before 2 August 2025 must comply by 2 August 2027.
signals_supported: EU AI Act high-risk regime postponement

publisher: NIST (Center for AI Standards and Innovation)
title: Announcing the AI Agent Standards Initiative for Interoperable and Secure Innovation
key_claim: CAISI launches AI Agent Standards Initiative covering industry-led agent standards, community-led open-source protocols, and research on agent security and identity infrastructure; first US government program dedicated to agentic AI interoperability and security.

title: Inside the AI Index: 12 Takeaways from the 2026 Report
key_claim: Foundation Model Transparency Index average scores dropped to 40 from 58; documented AI incidents rose to 362 in 2025 from 233 in 2024; US-China model performance gap effectively closed; Anthropic top model leads by 2.7%; US private AI investment $285.9bn in 2025.

publisher: International AI Safety Report (Bengio-chaired expert panel)
title: International AI Safety Report 2026: Extended Summary for Policymakers
key_claim: Second annual scientific synthesis from international expert panel on general-purpose AI risks; documents capability gains, governance gaps, and rising incident counts; commissioned by 30+ governments.

title: The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025
key_claim: Across 300+ AI initiatives, 52 structured interviews and 153 senior-leader survey responses (Jan-Jun 2025), 95% of generative AI pilots delivered no measurable P&L impact; purchasing from specialised vendors succeeds ~67% of the time vs internal builds at one-third that rate.

title: Tracking Trillions: The Assumptions Shaping the Scale of the AI Build-Out
key_claim: Projects $7.6 trillion cumulative AI capital expenditure 2026-2031; annual spending more than doubling from $765bn in 2026 to $1.6tn by 2031; maintaining returns would require ~$1tn annual profit run-rate, more than double 2026 consensus of $450bn.

title: Goldman finds no meaningful relationship between AI and productivity at the economy-wide level, but a 30% boost for two specific use cases
key_claim: Goldman Sachs Q4 earnings analysis: no meaningful AI-productivity link at economy-wide level; 70% of S&P 500 management teams discussed AI on calls but only 10% quantified impact on use cases and 1% on earnings; median 30% productivity gain where measured, concentrated in customer support and software development.

title: DeepSeek previews new AI model that closes the gap with frontier models
key_claim: DeepSeek V4 Preview released as open-weights with two variants (V4-Pro 1.6T total / 49B active; V4-Flash 284B / 13B active); claims reasoning performance approaching closed frontier models with 1M-token context windows.

title: AI Incident Roundup, November and December 2025 and January 2026
key_claim: 108 new incident IDs (1254 through 1361) added between November 2025 and end of January 2026; dominant thread is impersonation-for-profit and investment scams using familiar faces and formats.

title: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy: Version 3.0
key_claim: RSP v3.0 separates Anthropic's unilateral commitments from industry-wide recommendations; introduces Frontier Safety Roadmap and Risk Reports published every 3-6 months with external expert review; acknowledges higher-ASL safeguards may be infeasible unilaterally and require multilateral action.
